item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — Diuretic

lookback_source.quote: N0415G1. Diuretic: Check if a diuretic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

lookback_notes: 7-day look-back period, or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days. The manual uses "7-day look-back period" (N0415G1, p. N-7) and "observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)" (N0415G2, p. N-8) interchangeably; the item table on p. N-4 states "during the last 7 days or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days." The document does not state how the window is counted relative to the ARD on these pages.

coding_levels.label: Diuretic — Is taking
coding_levels.definition: Check if a diuretic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415G1. Diuretic: Check if a diuretic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Diuretic — Indication noted
coding_levels.definition: Check if there is an indication noted for all diuretic medications received by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415G2. Diuretic: Check if there is an indication noted for all diuretic medications received by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: None of the above
coding_levels.definition: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days). (Applies to the N0415 item as a whole, including the diuretic class.)

source.quote: N0415Z1. None of the above: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 2 (Indication noted) is coded only if Column 1 is checked: if Column 1 is checked, check whether an indication is noted for all medications in the drug class.

source.quote: Column 2: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used; Column 1 is checked if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

source.quote: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications with more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification are coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Long-acting medications given every few weeks or monthly are counted only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, capture the medication only if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications are coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products are dietary supplements and should not be counted as medications.

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately; use of the listed reference resources is not required for MDS completion.

source.quote: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately.

federal.criterion: Medical record documentation that the medication was received by the resident and documentation of the indication for its use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.notes: Step 1 of Steps for Assessment for N0415.

federal.criterion: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., medication given in the emergency room).

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.notes: Step 2 of Steps for Assessment for N0415.

federal.criterion: The indication must be the identified, documented clinical rationale for administering the medication, based on the prescriber's assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

source.quote: INDICATION The identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0 for pharmacological classification; facilities may wish to identify a consistently used resource.

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish") but states assessors should be able to identify the source used.

federal.criterion: Assessors may consult the manufacturer's package insert or work with the resident's pharmacist to confirm medication classification(s).

source.quote: Assessors should consult the manufacturer's package insert, which may contain the medication's pharmacological classification.

federal.notes: Suggested resource, not a required record.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied Section N pages do not tie N0415G (Diuretic) to any payment or case-mix classification.

conflicts.topic: Wording of the window for the Column 2 (indication noted) sub-item: "7-day look-back period" vs. "observation period"

positions.claim: N0415G1 states the window as the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415G1. Diuretic: Check if a diuretic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

positions.claim: N0415G2 states the window as "the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)" without repeating the 7-day figure.

source.quote: N0415G2. Diuretic: Check if there is an indication noted for all diuretic medications received by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the document: the general Coding Instructions define the observation period as 7 days — "Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)" (p. N-6).

conflicts.topic: Verb used for the diuretic indication sub-item: "received by" vs. "taken by" the resident

positions.claim: N0415G2 uses "received by the resident", unlike the other N0415 Column 2 sub-items.

source.quote: Check if there is an indication noted for all diuretic medications received by the resident any time during the observation period

positions.claim: Parallel Column 2 sub-items (e.g., N0415H2 Opioid) use "taken by the resident".

source.quote: N0415H2. Opioid: Check if there is an indication noted for all opioid medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period
